newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 58 perish in Delhi cinema fire.
newsitem.headline: At least 58 perish in Delhi cinema fire.

text.p: Fifty-eight people were killed on Friday when fire ripped through a packed cinema in the Indian capital.
Forty-one people died at one hospital and 17 at another, Tejinder Khanna, the lieutenant-governor of the nation's capital, told Reuters.
He said the fire started when an electrical transformer collapsed at the crowded Uphaar Grand cinema.
The blazing transformer set fire to dozens of cars parked in the cinema's basement.
Most of the dead were thought to have been sitting upstairs in the box and balcony sections, from where escape was harder, one fireman said. Most of those in the stalls were able to get out.
Eyewitnesses described horrific scenes. "I saw women with children in their arms breaking windows and jumping out. It was unbelievable," said one.
Khanna said all the cinema hall's documentation for fire standards was valid.
The cinema was packed to its capacity of 1,050 seats on the opening day of a popular new Hindi film, "Border", which dramatises a 1971 battle between India and Pakistan.
Hospital authorities said all the victims were dead on arrival, and most had died of suffocation.
Victims lay on trestle tables in the corridors of the capital's two biggest government-run hospitals as medical staff rushed from one to another with oxygen tanks.
"There are very few burns victims that have been brought to the hospital," S.P. Bajaj, additional medical superintendent at Safdurjung Hospital said.
"Most of the injured brought in a critical condition have stabilised now," said Ashok Kumar Sharma, chief medical officer of the hospital.
"The death toll is unlikely to rise dramatically," he said.
There were heart-rending scenes at the hospitals as relatives identified bodies. Several old women were crying as they searched through bodies lying on the floor.
Grieved relatives were desparately going through a list naming the dead stuck outside the entrance of Safdarjung Hospital.
The cinema was littered with glass and its walls blackened by the fire. Fire authorities feared the roof might cave in.
Rajesh Bhatia, one of the first to rush out when fire broke out said:" I broke one of the windows and jumped on to an adjoining roof when the commotion started."
"I think more people died in the stampede than due to burns."
The Delhi government announced compensation of 50,000 rupees ($1,400) to the families of each of the dead and 25,000 rupees to each person critically injured.
